summary.headline: Tata Technologies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.3% QoQ in constant currency to $175.4M (25.2% YoY), with management reiterating double-digit FY27 organic growth.
summary.overview:
Q1 FY27 revenue was $175.4M, up 4.3% QoQ and 25.2% YoY in constant currency, with Services at $136.6M (approximately 78% of revenue). Operating EBITDA was about $28M, a 16.1% margin, up 10 bps QoQ, while PBT fell to INR 252 crores from INR 283 crores because Q4 included a one-time Labour Code provision reversal. Management highlighted the $100M Tenneco engagement and a Japanese OEM full-vehicle program, and reiterated double-digit FY27 organic growth with growth expected to be much greater in H2 than H1. Near-term margin expansion may moderate due to upfront ramp-up investments and a Germany wage increase in Q2.</overview>

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Revenue $136.6M (approx. 78% of total), +4.3% QoQ cc and +24.4% YoY cc. Anchor-account share fell to 48.9%, down 150 bps QoQ; embedded and software grew 8.5% QoQ in USD.

segments.name: Technology Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue $38.8M, +4.2% QoQ cc and +27.9% YoY cc. Education grew 9.1% QoQ while product business declined 2.6% (seasonality); margin fell 250 bps on mix toward education.

segments.name: Automotive non-anchor
segments.commentary: Revenue $43.9M, +6.7% QoQ and +56.3% YoY. Non-anchor is about 49% of services revenue and about 36% of total automotive, per CFO.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: Revenue about $10.2M, +6.4% QoQ and +38.1% YoY. Management sees a path to a $100M target in the next two to three years.

segments.name: IHM
segments.commentary: Revenue about $15M; no growth rate was disclosed on the call.

segments.name: Europe (geography)
segments.commentary: Revenue about $67.9M, +10.1% QoQ, supported by Es-Tec integration; Germany saw an uptick, but some customers are under restructuring.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: strong double-digit organic revenue growth, with services as the primary growth engine; management reiterated this on the call.
Growth is expected to be much greater in H2 than H1 FY27, with the ramp-up of closed deals as the main driver; quarterly phasing depends on team mobilisation and customer readiness.
Management said it would not focus on a specific margin milestone; it expects QoQ margin expansion to continue in Q2 despite the annual wage increase in Q2.
Tenneco ($100M, 5-year deal) begins execution in Q2, scales toward calendar year-end, and will require incremental headcount and cost.
Management said Germany wage increases in Q2 will be absorbed, which may moderate the pace of margin expansion near term.
capex_capacity: Several large strategic engagements and full-vehicle programs entered mobilisation in Q1, requiring upfront investment in talent, ramp-up, transition and delivery readiness ahead of steady-state revenue.
BMW TechWorks crossed 2,000 engineers; it is a JV and not consolidated into revenue.
Headcount optimised to 12,579 with a balanced FTE vs outsourced mix; hiring is selective and focused on strategic skill areas.
Development cycles of 18 to 24 months for full vehicles, versus 36 to 48 months at many Western OEMs, per management.
demand_pricing: Tenneco: $100M multiyear transformation engagement spanning engineering, digital, AI-enabled processes and operational modernisation; described as mostly new business with a small renewal element.
A North American industrial equipment manufacturer engagement covering systems, software and embedded software, using AI-enabled methodologies.
A leading global OEM Range Extender Vehicle program; a leading off-highway manufacturer selected Tata Technologies as preferred partner.
A Japanese OEM full-vehicle development program, which management described as a first-time relationship in this space and a path into Japan.
Management said deal momentum continued into Q2 and that additional large deals have closed beyond those disclosed; no customer names or sizes were given.
Management said tariffs and EV tapering had held back demand over the past ~18 months, and that clarity is now returning and investment is resuming.
On AI pricing, management said AI is a force multiplier on productivity and that it sees the work volume as expanding, not shrinking.
